newsitem.title: UK: Routine hedging fails to add value - WM research.
newsitem.headline: Routine hedging fails to add value - WM research.

text.p: Systematic hedging by international bond managers is failing to deliver satisfactory results, reducing variability but at the expense of performance, according to research by The WM Company.
Significant added value from hedging arises only if a major movement in currencies occurs such as the shifts in the fourth quarter of 1992, WM said.

Their research covered fixed income portfolios in a universe of 15 eligible funds with a total aggregate market value of $5.0 billion. Ten investment management organisations were represented and the analysis was over a five year period ending December 1995.

"Relative to an unhedged position variability has been significantly reduced but a one percent per annum markdown in return over the three years to the end of December 1995 may not be acceptable to even the most cautious and conservative of investors," WM said.
Director Colin Kay said the analysis suggested that by giving managers discretion to hedge, "the chances are they will lose money on it".
"The bottom line is that if you are looking for value on the currency side make sure that what has been promised is actually delivered."
